QF.id: Cat III AIF Due Diligence and Risk_12

question.text: Fund Size / AUM is a relevant DD consideration because:

answer.text: Too-small AUM may indicate illiquidity risk; too-large AUM may signal strategy capacity constraints

explanation.text: The Logic: Fund size / AUM matters in two directions during distributor due diligence. A very small AUM can raise concerns about operational viability, fee economics, and the ability to absorb redemptions without forced selling — pointing to illiquidity and going-concern risk. A very large AUM, on the other hand, can stretch a strategy beyond its natural capacity (especially for alpha-driven Cat III strategies), diluting returns and forcing the manager into less attractive opportunities. "Bigger is always better" misses the capacity ceiling, and AUM is not relevant only for fees or operational cost. The Trap: Monotonic interpretations (bigger-is-better) miss the nuance — the relevance is two-sided. Note: The specific two-sided framing — too-small AUM indicating illiquidity risk and too-large AUM signalling strategy capacity constraints — is not stated in the NISM Series XIX-B AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook pages checked; the framing above reflects general industry due-diligence practice for hedge-fund-style strategies rather than a workbook citation.
